version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: take a cpuset cookie for the interleave node count

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a memory allocation bug in the Linux kernel's mempolicy module by taking a cpuset cookie around the count of nodes to be allocated from. The bug occurs when a concurrent cpuset rebind can cause a torn read of the nodemask, leading to an empty mask and incorrect allocation. The patch introduces a retry mechanism to ensure that the nodemask is valid before proceeding with the allocation. This fix has been measured to reduce zero counts by 87% in a 72-node VM.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 01/14] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to an O(N * M) nested loop. The limit is set at NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024), which is considered far above any realistic configuration. The patch also adds a check for oversized listener lists before taking any locks, ensuring that the system remains secure and responsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 02/14] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch validates the transport name in the listener_set function before server creation to prevent arbitrary names from reaching svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). The validation checks if the name matches one of the supported transport classes (tcp, udp, or rdma) and rejects any unsupported names. This narrows the scope of a TASK_KILLABLE usermode helper upcall that can be triggered under nfsd_mutex. The patch also ensures that NFSD accepts 'rdma' without condition, even if svcrdma is not built, to allow for modular autoload in the kernel.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 03/14] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the svc_register() function where it returns the last error encountered, overwriting any earlier failures. Instead, it keeps track of the first error and returns that. This ensures that all errors are preserved and can be reported to the user.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 04/14] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The kernel's current behavior allows a stalled connection to cause a long hold on nfsd_mutex, potentially triggering the hung-task watchdog. By capping the timeout at 1 second, the patch reduces the likelihood of this issue occurring. However, it does not eliminate the problem entirely and registration remains synchronous and fatal. A more comprehensive fix would be to make the registration asynchronous.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 05/14] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the error reporting in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) listener creation process by providing more detailed information to userland when a failure occurs. Specifically, it records and reports the attribute and transport name of the entry that failed, allowing for better diagnosis and troubleshooting. The patch modifies the nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit function to set an extack with the relevant error message and details after each loop iteration.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 06/14] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new error code, -ENAVAIL, to indicate that an rpcbind call received no answer. It also adds a counter, sv_rpcb_failures, to track the number of unanswered calls. The caller can use this count to determine if there have been any errors. This change is intended to improve the handling of rpcbind failures and provide more information to callers about the status of their requests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 07/14] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs and versions when the local rpcbind client times out, rather than continuing to try other programs and versions. This change is intended to prevent unnecessary delays and improve performance. The patch achieves this by adding a check for no response from the rpcbind client and breaking out of the program loop if it occurs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 08/14] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC service to stop clearing rpcbind entries after the first call that receives no answer from rpcbind. This change is intended to prevent unnecessary timeouts and improve performance when a local rpcbind never replies.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 09/14] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused each listener to wait for a timeout, leading to unnecessary delays and potential failures in the teardown process. To address this issue, the patch introduces a new function `svc_xprt_clear_rpcb_unreg` that clears the flag indicating that rpcbind is unresponsive on remaining listeners when the first failure occurs. This change improves the efficiency of the listener destruction process and reduces the likelihood of further failures during teardown.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 10/14] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code, where a silent rpcbind failure can cause the nfsd_mutex to be held for an extended period of time. The patch introduces a check for rpcbind failures and, if one occurs, it skips registering with rpcbind for subsequent listeners. This approach prevents the mutex from being held indefinitely and allows the system to recover more quickly in case of a failure.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 11/14] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests to the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to exercise listener_set request validation. The tests cover various invalid scenarios, such as bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use a stub to create a service and run in their own network namespace. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds new directories to the NFSD test suite.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 12/14] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-network namespace (netns) rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd test suite. The stub serves rpcbind from within the netns, allowing tests to register listeners and round-trip requests without relying on the host's rpcbind service. This is necessary because a fresh netns has no rpcbind service, causing registration failures and timeouts. The patch also includes new tests that cover various scenarios, including listener creation, addition, removal, and IPv6 support.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 13/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) selftest suite to ensure that listener_set requests only ask rpcbind once. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener after failure, silent set completion, and version set only. New functions are introduced to handle these cases, including RPCB_STUB_SILENT and version_set_only(). The patch aims to prevent multiple calls to rpcbind for each request, which would lead to inefficiencies in the system.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 14/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to ensure that removing multiple listeners from the NFS daemon does not result in multiple timeouts for rpcbind. The test creates one listener, then three listeners while the stub is silent, and measures the number of calls made to rpcbind during each removal. It checks that the second and third removals do not reach rpcbind at all, thus preventing unnecessary timeouts.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to harden the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon (nfsd) and sunrpc code. The main goal is to prevent unnecessary timeouts when communicating with rpcbind, which can lead to hangs and other issues. The patches introduce several changes to improve the registration and deregistration of listeners, including stopping the registration process once rpcbind stops answering.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton
review_comments.summary: Posted the patch series for review, highlighting its focus on hardening the netlink listener set interface and preventing unnecessary timeouts when communicating with rpcbind.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 16 +++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index 5331b89c4281..b6f4d66f612a 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,21 +1995,22 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
+#define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
+
 /**
  * nfsd_nl_validate_listeners - sanity-check the listener list from userland
  * @info: netlink metadata and command arguments
  *
- * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that each entry
- * is well-formed: it parses against the policy, carries both an address and
- * a transport name, and the address is long enough for its family. Doing
- * this up front lets the callers below assume every entry is valid and
- * guarantees we make no changes when the request is malformed.
+ * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that the list is
+ * not oversized and that each entry is well-formed.
  *
  * Return: 0 if every entry is valid, or a negative errno otherwise.
  */
 static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 {
 	const struct nlattr *attr;
+	unsigned int count = 0;
 	int rem;
 
 	nlmsg_for_each_attr_type(attr, NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR, info->nlhdr,
@@ -2018,6 +2019,11 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		struct sockaddr *sa;
 		int err;
 
+		if (++count > NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG(info->extack, "too many listeners");
+			return -E2BIG;
+		}
+
 		err = nla_parse_nested(tb, NFSD_A_SOCK_MAX, attr,
 				       nfsd_sock_nl_policy, info->extack);
 		if (err < 0)

review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is
necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=c7eae0eb80858a2dba0f
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 24 ++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 24 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index b6f4d66f612a..d8135f38e69f 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,6 +1995,23 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Transport classes NFSD knows how to instantiate. Vetting the name here
+ * keeps a bogus string from reaching svc_xprt_create_from_sa(), where an
+ * unknown name triggers a request_module("svc%s", name) upcall under
+ * nfsd_mutex.
+ */
+static bool nfsd_nl_transport_supported(const char *name)
+{
+	static const char * const supported[] = { "tcp", "udp", "rdma" };
+	int i;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(supported); i++)
+		if (!strcmp(name, supported[i]))
+			return true;
+	return false;
+}
+
 /* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
 #define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
 
@@ -2032,6 +2049,13 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		if (!tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR] || !tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME])
 			return -EINVAL;
 
+		if (!nfsd_nl_transport_supported(nla_data(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME]))) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG_ATTR(info->extack,
+					    tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME],
+					    "unsupported transport name");
+			return -EPROTONOSUPPORT;
+		}
+
 		sa = nla_data(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR]);
 		if (nla_len(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR]) < sizeof(sa->sa_family))
 			return -EINVAL;

review_comments.raw_body:
The kernel's local rpcbind client uses the transport defaults: a 10s major
timeout for AF_LOCAL, and 60s for the loopback TCP fallback.
xprt_calc_majortimeo() returns to_initval when to_increment is 0.

Those calls are synchronous, and they run under nfsd_mutex. One operation
makes several of them. rpcb_create_local() tries up to three client
creations, and svc_register() sends one call for each program and version.
A local rpcbind that accepts the connection but never replies stalls every
one of these calls. The accumulated hold is long enough to trip the
hung-task watchdog on other NFSD netlink operations. The holder itself
waits killably and escapes the watchdog:

  INFO: task hung in nfsd_nl_cache_flush_doit

The local rpcbind is on loopback or on an AF_LOCAL socket, and it answers
in microseconds. Bound its client to one attempt of 1s.

This shortens the stall. It does not remove the stall, and it is not free.
Registration stays synchronous and stays fatal. An rpcb_create_local()
failure aborts nfsd_create_serv() through svc_bind(), and an
svc_register() failure makes svc_setup_socket() fail. An rpcbind that is
merely slow to be scheduled can therefore now fail server startup, where
it succeeded before. The real fix is to make the registration
asynchronous.

Assisted-by: LLM
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=c7eae0eb80858a2dba0f
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c | 12 ++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)

diff --git a/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c b/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
index 6aa372188c86..0aa376b82a52 100644
--- a/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
+++ b/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
@@ -221,6 +221,16 @@ static void rpcb_set_local(struct net *net, struct rpc_clnt *clnt,
 # define SUN_LEN(ptr) (offsetof(struct sockaddr_un, sun_path)		\
 		      + 1 + strlen((ptr)->sun_path + 1))
 
+/*
+ * The kernel's rpcbind client talks only to the local rpcbind, over loopback
+ * or a local AF_LOCAL socket, where a healthy rpcbind answers in microseconds.
+ */
+static const struct rpc_timeout rpcb_local_timeout = {
+	.to_initval	= 1 * HZ,
+	.to_maxval	= 1 * HZ,
+	.to_retries	= 0,
+};
+
 /*
  * Returns zero on success, otherwise a negative errno value
  * is returned.
@@ -238,6 +248,7 @@ static int rpcb_create_af_local(struct net *net,
 		.version	= RPCBVERS_2,
 		.authflavor	= RPC_AUTH_NULL,
 		.cred		= current_cred(),
+		.timeout	= &rpcb_local_timeout,
 		/*
 		 * We turn off the idle timeout to prevent the kernel
 		 * from automatically disconnecting the socket.
@@ -312,6 +323,7 @@ static int rpcb_create_local_net(struct net *net)
 		.version	= RPCBVERS_2,
 		.authflavor	= RPC_AUTH_UNIX,
 		.cred		= current_cred(),
+		.timeout	= &rpcb_local_timeout,
 		.flags		= RPC_CLNT_CREATE_NOPING,
 	};
 	struct rpc_clnt *clnt, *clnt4;

review_comments.summary: Addressed Jeff's concerns, noting that reconnect storms are rare and that NFSv4.1 provides a total solution for the issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, Aug 28, 2026, at 3:15 PM, Jeff Layton wrote:
> On Fri, 2026-08-28 at 14:59 -0400, Chuck Lever wrote:
>> On Fri, Aug 28, 2026, at 2:38 PM, Jeff Layton wrote:
>> > On Fri, 2026-08-28 at 12:17 -0400, Chuck Lever wrote:
>> > > A completed DRC entry stays in its bucket until RC_EXPIRE elapses or
>> > > the cache exceeds max_drc_entries. Entries whose replies the client
>> > > already holds lengthen the bucket and slow every lookup that hashes
>> > > there.
>> > > 
>> > > RFC 1813 Section 4.5 observes that on a connection-oriented transport
>> > > a duplicate request arises from reconnection, not from within a live
>> > > connection. A fresh request on a live TCP or RDMA connection therefore
>> > > means the client is not retransmitting an earlier one. UDP clients
>> > > retransmit on timeout over a shared svc_xprt, so eviction is
>> > > restricted to transports marked XPT_ORDERED. Even there the evidence
>> > > is not conclusive, since a client with several requests outstanding
>> > > sends the next before the previous reply arrives. The cache is
>> > > advisory: a premature eviction costs a miss and re-execution, the same
>> > > outcome memory pressure and RC_EXPIRE already produce.
>> > 
>> > No, it's not. The DRC is necessary for proper function, and if we drop
>> > non-idempotent requests prematurely, then that could cause spurious
>> > errors.
>> > 
>> > Or am I misunderstanding what you mean by "The cache" here?
>> 
>> Not talking about the NFSv4.1 session cache. The old DRC has
>> always been best-effort. It cannot be relied upon for proper
>> function, since the DRC is non-deterministic.
>> 
>
> Yes, but in this case you can potentially evict this thing well before
> you actually need it:
>
> - client does a v3 RENAME (anything non-idempotent, really)
> - reply to the RENAME goes out just before a new call comes in (WRITE
> or something maybe). The RENAME DRC entry's timestamp is a few jiffies
> earlier so we evict it.
> - connection drops before client gets the reply and client reconnects
> and retransmits the v3 RENAME
>
> ...hilarity ensues? Maybe this sort of bad luck never happens in
> practice, but I don't see what would prevent it.

The same thing can happen if NFSD is handling a thousand chatty
clients. With fast networks and fast storage, overrunning the DRC
is more likely than it ever has been.

I've got more patches that moderate this behavior some. I could
post those as well... I was hoping to keep the patch sets narrow
to avoid overwhelming reviewers.


>> The point I'm making here is that items already get evicted
>> due to memory pressure or because the DRC size is capped.
>> 
>> In particular, if you are actively removing items that are
>> very unlikely to be hit, that *reduces* the likelihood that
>> other, perhaps more valuable, items will be evicted due to
>> memory pressure.
>> 
>
> Sure, but usually we evict the oldest stuff first, and we generally
> keep a big enough cache to get past the point where retransmissions
> occur. This patchset changes that and will evict things earlier.
>
> Maybe that's OK in practice.

The reconnect case is the only one I'm really concerned about.
I'm not brushing aside your concern, but missing a non-idempotent
reply during a reconnect storm is somewhat rare, and is already
not 100% deterministic.

And we have NFSv4.1 now. For anyone who is deeply concerned
about this race, NFSv4.1 is the only total answer.

-- 
Chuck Lever

patches_reviewed.subject: Re: memcg stats flushing (WAS "Re: [PATCH] fuse: disable default bdi strictlimiting")
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch addresses the issue of high overhead in memcg stats flushing, particularly at high depths (8-16) where the extra latency can be up to 48ns. The problem arises from the use of rstat rate-limiting, which is arbitrary and bounded by time rather than actual stats updates. The proposed solution involves minimizing unnecessary overhead by not updating stats that don't require precision, and removing the rate-limiting mechanism. This approach aims to strike a balance between precision and performance, especially in scenarios where lock contention is a concern.

Yeah it could be a problem, but I think we won't know for sure until

actually shows up (or doesn't) in higher-level workloads.

per-memcg thresholding), we ran into hard lockups for flushes taking

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/5] mm/huge_memory: do not touch frozen folios in deferred_split_isolate()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the deferred_split_isolate() function in the Linux kernel's huge_memory module to avoid touching folios that are frozen by calling folio_ref_freeze(). The current implementation treats a zero refcount as an indication that the folio is going away, but this can lead to unnecessary unqueuing of folios. The patch introduces a check for the folio being under folio_ref_freeze() and skips it instead of trying to isolate it. This change ensures that the owner of the frozen folio is responsible for its fate and prevents unnecessary unqueuing.

Right, IIUC, we have two options so far:

A) Conservatively reject collapse for any UFFD-minor-registered VMA, as

B) Allow collapse when the workload itself asks for it, but reject

deciding what the check should look like.

distinction is only between the workload's own madvise(MADV_COLLAPSE)

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm, swap: fix SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT collision with real usage count

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a collision between the SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT flag and the real usage count in the Linux kernel's swap management code. The issue occurs when the system has 4 KiB pages, causing bit 30 to be set in the usage counter, which is meant to sit above any value that counter can reach. This leads to incorrect reporting of used space in /proc/swaps and potential data corruption during swapoff operations. To fix this, the patch changes the definition of SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT to use atomic_long_t instead of atomic_t, ensuring it sits above the maximum possible usage count.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 01/11] mm, swap: add virtual swap device infrastructure
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces the virtual swap device infrastructure, which allows for dynamic allocation of swap space and enables features like zswap and zero-filled pages without a physical swap device. The virtual swap device is created when the 'vswap' kernel parameter is set to 'on', and it lives for the lifetime of the kernel. The patch also includes changes to various files such as mm/swap.h, mm/page_io.c, and mm/vswap.h to support this new infrastructure. The dynamic-cluster allocator is wired in, but no allocation path can select it yet, with subsequent patches expected to add the necessary paths.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 02/11] mm, swap: support zswap and zero-filled swap pages as vswap backends
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds support for zswap and zero-filled swap pages as virtual swap (vswap) backends, allowing compressed or zero-filled pages to be stored without pre-allocating physical swap slots. The vswap layer decouples PTE swap entries from physical backing, enabling efficient compression and detection of zero-filled pages. However, this patch only supports zswap and zero-page backends, with physical disk backing and real writeback to be implemented in later patches. Additionally, THP (Transparent Huge Pages) swapin is disabled for vswap entries until further development.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 03/11] mm, swap: prepare the swap IO path for vswap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prepares the Linux kernel's swap IO path to support virtual swap (vswap) by allowing it to submit IO for a swap entry other than folio->swap. The current implementation derives the target device and sector from folio->swap, which is not suitable for vswap entries backed by physical slots. To address this, the patch introduces a new field in the swap_iocb structure to store the sector of the swap entry, and updates various functions to use this new field instead of folio->swap. This change enables the batching path to serve both vswap entries and physical entries mapped directly into PTEs without any functional changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 04/11] mm, swap: support physical swap as a vswap backend
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds support for physical swap as a backend for the virtual swap layer, allowing zswap to decline pages and allocate physical slots on demand. The physical slot is tracked via a pointer-tagged swap_table entry, and readahead scans are modified to skip these entries. The patch also includes changes to handle failed reads of vswap entries and to bypass vswap when zswap is disabled at the host level or for the folio's cgroup.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 05/11] mm, swap: enable THP swapin for vswap entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch enables the swapping in of large anonymous memory pages (THP) for vswap entries when they share a contiguous run of physical swap slots on a synchronous IO device. This allows for more efficient swapping and reduces the number of faults that occur during the process. The patch also introduces checks to ensure that zswap-backed or mixed-backing batches are not swapped in as THPs, and that fault retries occur at smaller orders when necessary.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 06/11] mm, swap: write back vswap zswap entries to physical swap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds support for writing back zswap-backed vswap entries to physical swap. It mirrors the existing zswap writeback path, but allocates physical backing on demand at writeback time instead of pre-allocating it. The zswap shrinker no longer skips vswap entries unless there is not enough physical swap space available. This allows for more efficient use of swap space and improves system performance.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 07/11] mm, swap: reclaim physical slots backing cache-only vswap entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch reclaims physical slots backing cache-only vswap entries when the swap is more than half used. Cache-only vswap entries are those where the vswap entry's swap_count has dropped to 0, but its folio is still in the swap cache. The patch introduces a new flag, SWP_RMAP_CACHE_ONLY, to mark such entries and allows reclaiming their physical slots from the physical reclaim scanner. This change aims to free up physical capacity for new allocations when the swap usage exceeds half of the available space.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 08/11] mm, swap: only charge physical swap entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the way memory swap is charged to a cgroup's memcg->swap counter. Instead of charging when a vswap entry is allocated, it charges only when the entry acquires physical backing. This change ensures that zswap-backed and zero-filled pages are not counted towards the cgroup's swap usage. The patch also refactors the swap memcg operations into separate helpers for getting, recording, charging, uncharging, and putting the owner, which is a prerequisite for this change. As a result, memory.swap.current will only count on-disk swap usage, allowing cgroups to reclaim their anon memory even with memory.swap.max set to 0 if zswap is enabled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 09/11] mm, swap: add debugfs counters for vswap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds two debugfs counters to track virtual swap usage in the Linux kernel. The first counter, 'used', tracks the number of virtual swap slots (pages) currently allocated. The second counter, 'alloc_reject', counts the cumulative number of pages that failed to get a vswap slot. These counters are exposed under the '/sys/kernel/debug/vswap/' directory and provide visibility into virtual swap allocation behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 10/11] mm, swap: defer memcg_table allocation for physical swap clusters
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes memory allocation for swap clusters by deferring the allocation of a memcg table until it's actually needed. This is done to reduce unnecessary memory usage in cases where a physical swap cluster only holds vswap backings, which don't require a memcg table. The patch allocates the table eagerly for vswap clusters and for physical clusters when vswap is disabled or not enabled. Otherwise, allocation is deferred until the first direct-use slot is handed out.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 11/11] mm, swap: widen swap_info_struct max/pages to unsigned long
series_items.patch_summary: This patch widens the size of swap_info_struct's max and pages fields from unsigned int to unsigned long, allowing the vswap device to exceed its previous 16 TB capacity limit when using 4 KB pages. The new maximum capacity is determined by the cluster_info_pool xarray's allocator limit, which can store up to ~8 PB at a typical SWAPFILE_CLUSTER=512 layout. This change enables larger swap devices and improves system performance for systems with high memory demands.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series introduces Virtual Swap Space (VSwap), a new feature that allows for efficient and scalable swapping by decoupling swap entries from their backing storage. The current implementation ties swap entries to their backing slot, which can lead to performance issues when swap is used as a cache or when swapoff is frequent. VSwap addresses these issues by introducing a separate data structure for swap entries, allowing for more flexible and efficient management of swap space.

On Thu, Aug 27, 2026 at 05:13:44PM -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:

> > A non-blocking charge can hit the limit, get rejected, but is not
> > visible in memory.events.
> > 
> > This was noticed in a production setting where bpf_mem_alloc() attempted
> > to refill its per-cpu freelists, which triggered a non-blocking charge
> > while at the limit.
> >
